patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches show a persistent header/navigation area at the top separated from the page content by a horizontal rule, suggesting the top bar remains available while reading a long article.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Header should remain fixed or sticky during scroll so branding/navigation stays accessible across the long-form article layout.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly show scrolling states, so this could also be a static header; stickiness is inferred from the blog/article pattern and top-bar treatment.

sketch_notes: The sketches primarily depict a static article page with related content cards and footer links, with very little explicit interactive UI beyond standard link navigation. No hamburger, dropdowns, forms, tabs, accordions, modals, or loading mechanisms are visibly indicated. The only JavaScript-relevant behavior strongly implied across viewports is a sticky top navigation/header treatment for a long scrolling reading experience; otherwise the page appears largely content-driven and could be implemented mostly without JavaScript.
